This book covers Chapter 1, "Exploration: Entering the World of Secondary Science" (how science works: models, laws, theories, SI units, estimation and prediction) and Chapter 5, "Exploring Mixtures and Their Separation" (pure substances and mixtures, solutions, suspensions, colloids, the Tyndall effect and separation techniques).

All numerical answers have been checked by computer. The marking points are our own, not an official CBSE marking scheme. Use your Exploration textbook alongside.

Unit 1 of 10: How Science Works

Key ideas

  • Science is a way of finding out about the natural world through observation, questioning, testing and reasoning.
  • A common sequence: observe → ask a question → form a hypothesis → test by experiment → analyse data → conclude → share and review.
  • A hypothesis is a testable explanation; an experiment changes one variable (independent), measures another (dependent) and keeps others controlled.
  • Scientific knowledge is tentative — it can change with new evidence.

Worked examples

Example 1: Riya tests whether plants grow taller with more sunlight. Name the independent and dependent variables. Answer: independent — amount of sunlight; dependent — plant height.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) A testable explanation for an observation is a: (a) law (b) hypothesis (c) unit (d) conclusion. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) Why is science called "tentative"? Answer: it can change when new evidence appears.
  3. (2 marks) In Riya's experiment, name two variables she must keep constant. Answer: water given (1); type of plant / soil (1).
  4. (3 marks) Arrange the steps: conclude, hypothesis, observe, experiment. Explain why repeating an experiment matters. Answer: observe → hypothesis → experiment → conclude (1); repetition reduces chance errors (1); makes results reliable (1).
  5. (3 marks) A student says, "Heavier objects always fall faster." Suggest how to test this fairly. Answer: drop objects of different mass from the same height (1); keep shape/air resistance similar (1); time the falls several times and compare (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Hypothesis = fact. 2. Changing many variables at once. 3. No controls. 4. Single trials. 5. Conclusions beyond the data.

Quick recall

  1. Testable explanation? 2. Variable changed? 3. Variable measured? 4. Kept same? 5. Science is?

Answers: 1) Hypothesis. 2) Independent. 3) Dependent. 4) Controlled. 5) Tentative.
